1. Heard Shri Aman Kumar Shrivastav, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Diwakar Singh,
learned Aga for the State-respondents.
2. Despite service of notice upon opposite party no.2, no one has appeared on her behalf.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant has been falsely implicated
and is in jail since 02.12.2018 in Case Crime No.974 of 2018 under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) Ipc
and Section 3/4(2) Pocso Act and Section 3(2)(5) Sc/St Act, police station Kotwali Sadar, District
Kheri.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court to impugned FIR, wherein the date of incident is 18.08.2018 and the FIR has been lodged on 24.08.2018, without explaining the aforesaid delay.
The allegation has been levelled against six accused persons including the present applicant.

5. Learned counsel has further stated that despite the fact that the prosecutrix has levelled specific allegation upon co-accused Rampyari, Deendayal, Sandeep and Chhotelal for kidnapping her, but charge sheet has been filed only against the present applicant.

Attention has also been drawn towards statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., wherein she has not levelled any allegation against present applicant in respect of rape and if her statements are taken on its face value, the offence of kidnapping has not been committed by the present applicant and those persons who have kidnapped the prosecutrix, charge sheet has not been filed against them.
Learned trial Court has framed charges against the applicant on 17.07.2019 under Sections 363, 366 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act, but no charge has been framed under Section 376 IPC.

While recording the Chief of the prosecutrix, the allegation of rape against the present applicant has been pointed out, but during the course of cross-examination, she did not level any allegation against the present applicant regarding rape.

Initially, the trial was before the Special Court dealing with the matter of SC/ST Act, but after imposition of Section 376(3) IPC and Section 3/4(2) POCSO Act, the trial would be conducted by the Special Court dealing with issues of POCSO Act.
6.

Learned counsel for the applicant has lastly submitted that in the aforesaid circumstances, there is no possibility of conclusion of trial very soon, therefore, considering the total period of incarceration of present applicant, that is more than six years, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

He further submits that the applicant has no criminal history and if the present applicant be enlarged on bail, he undertakes that he shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
Further, the applicant shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order.
7. Learned AGA has, however, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant.

8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the material on record, it transpires that the no allegation of rape was levelled against the applicant in statement recorded by the prosecutrix in her statement under Sections 161, 164 Cr.P.C. and she levelled allegation of rape against the applicant only in her Chief but again in cross examination the applicant did not level any allegation of rape against the applicant, the applicant has no criminal history, therefore, without entering into merits of the issue; considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties;
contents and allegations of the FIR and undertaking of the applicant that he shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail, I find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail.
9. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let applicant- Dinesh Sharma be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
11. Learned trial Court is directed to conduct and conclude the trial, expeditiously and without giving any unnecessary adjournments to any of the parties.
(Rajesh Singh Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 12.12.2024
